title: Relative Serre vanishing for a proper morphism
statement: Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], let $f:X\to S$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], let $\mathcal F$ be a quasi-coherent coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent], and let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module] such that, for every affine open $V\subseteq S$, the restriction $\mathcal L|_{f^{-1}(V)}$ is ample [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Then there is an integer $n_0$ such that $R^p f_*(\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes n})=0$ for every $n\ge n_0$ and every $p>0.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 30.17.1 (Tag 02O1), label lemma-kill-by-twisting

proof.text: Let V be any affine open of S, let j:V \to S be its inclusion, and put X_V = X \times_S V with induced morphism f_V:X_V \to V. Properness of f is preserved by this base change [lem-pc-proper-base-change]. By the definition of proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism], f_V is separated and of finite type, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Since S is Noetherian, V = Spec(A) has Noetherian coordinate ring; the restriction F_V is coherent and the restriction L_V is ample on X_V by the hypotheses and the definitions. Thus the affine-base Serre-vanishing statement [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-serre-vanishing] applies to f_V, F_V, and L_V.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 30.17.1 (Tag 02O1), proof: reduction to affine opens of the base

proof.text: For each affine V from Step 1, choose n_V such that H^p(X_V, F_V tensor L_V^n) = 0 for every p > 0 and n >= n_V. The affine-base comparison [lem-pc-cohomology-sections-affine-base] identifies this group with Gamma(V, R^p(f_V)_*(F_V tensor L_V^n)), so these sections vanish for all p > 0 and n >= n_V. The higher direct image is quasi-coherent by [lem-pc-finite-support-hi] (1), and a quasi-coherent module on an affine scheme whose global sections vanish is zero, by the affine tilde-global-sections equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] (3). Hence R^p(f_V)_*(F_V tensor L_V^n) = 0 for all p > 0 and n >= n_V.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 30.17.1 (Tag 02O1), proof: affine-base vanishing and Lemma 01XK

proof.text: For E_n = F tensor L^{tensor n}, restriction of the derived direct image to V is canonically Rf_*E_n|_V isomorphic to R(f_V)_*(E_n|_{X_V}) by [lem-pc-restrict-derived-direct-image-open]. Taking p-th cohomology sheaves and using Step 2 gives (R^p f_*E_n)|_V = 0 for every p > 0 and n >= n_V.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 30.17.1 (Tag 02O1), proof: passage from affine restrictions to higher direct images

proof.text: Because S is Noetherian, choose a finite affine open cover S = \bigcup_j V_j. For each V_j, Steps 1--3 give a bound n_{V_j}; set n_0 = \max_j n_{V_j}. Then Step 3 shows (R^p f_*E_n)|_{V_j} = 0 for every p > 0 and n >= n_0. A sheaf whose restrictions vanish on an open cover is zero, so R^p f_*E_n = 0 for every p > 0 and n >= n_0. This proves the asserted bound.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 30.17.1 (Tag 02O1), conclusion after the affine-local reduction
